reference: Bash type/help builtin contracts and util-linux column for runnable parity. Parity cases run the same deterministic script on both shells with private relative fixture files; expected behavior is not derived from bash-os output.
coverage: Bash metadata: column is registered as a builtin and help -s advertises its documented synopsis.
util-linux table output with default whitespace separators, ragged rows, explicit field separators, empty fields, and a custom output separator.
util-linux non-table layout with explicit output width, column-first versus row-first filling, and explicit space padding.
Named relative file operands, an unterminated final input record, repeated redirected stdin in one shell, and invalid output-width handling.
Nonempty zero-width list and table modes, ragged explicitly separated tails, repeated dash operands, and a custom identity banner.
exclusions: Only the column command is covered; the sibling col and colrm builtins are outside this suite.
Terminal-derived default width, wide-character display alignment, and util-linux options outside the implemented column subset are not covered.
No privileged, host-system, hardware, or network operation is part of column's selected behavior, so no operation case is deferred.

cases.purpose: Use Bash's type -t contract to confirm that the statically registered column command is recognized as a builtin with an empty candidate PATH.
Check that Bash help exposes the registered column synopsis and includes its documented table and row-fill options.
cases.script:
synopsis=$(help -s column)
if [[ $synopsis == *column* && $synopsis == *-x* && $synopsis == *-t* ]]; then
  printf '%s\n' 'column synopsis advertised'
else
  printf '%s\n' 'column synopsis missing' >&2
  exit 1
fi

cases.purpose: Compare table mode's default whitespace splitting and column alignment across mixed spaces, tabs, leading whitespace, and a shorter final row.
cases.script:
printf '  NAME	AGE  CITY  
Al 8 NY
Beatrice	12	Los Angeles
Cy 4
' > rows.txt
column -t < rows.txt

cases.purpose: Compare colon-separated table parsing, preservation of empty fields between adjacent separators, and a multi-byte output separator.
Compare non-table vertical filling at an explicit width with deterministic short items and a final incomplete row.
Compare -x row-first item ordering against the same explicit-width non-table fixture.
Compare the implemented --use-spaces padding mode at a fixed output width instead of tab-separated columns.
Compare table input from two private relative file operands, including a final record without a newline.
cases.script:
printf 'key value\nshort 1' > first.txt
printf 'longer 22\n' > second.txt
column -t first.txt second.txt

cases.purpose: Run column repeatedly in one shell with fresh redirections to the same relative file; each invocation must independently process all rows.
cases.script:
printf 'alpha\nbeta\n' > repeated.txt
for pass in 1 2 3; do column -t < repeated.txt; done

cases.purpose: Zero width is accepted with empty stdin; the separate nonempty case determines its formatting behavior.
Exercise zero width with nonempty list and table input; raw formatting is compared.
cases.script:
printf 'one\ntwo\nthree\n' > items
column -c 0 items
column -x --output-width=0 items
column -t --output-width 0 items

cases.purpose: Missing cells must retain padding and separators through the final table column.
Keep the existing bash-loadable identity banner as a custom contract, separate from external version output.
Repeated dash operands share stdin once per invocation; each fresh redirection reads the complete stream. Expected bytes follow the documented logical-stream extension.
cases.script:
printf 'A' > input
column -t - - < input
column -t - - < input

cases.purpose: Whitespace-only records are ignored (column manual); actual ragged records retain their missing-cell padding. Compare default and explicit separators plus list mode without trimming output.
cases.script:
printf 'a:b:c

   
long:z
:
' > input
column -ts: input
printf 'a b c

	
long z
' | column -t
printf 'one

   
two
' | column -c 0

cases.purpose: Empty input is empty; negative output width is rejected diagnostically.
Ordinary negative widths fail with util-linux status 1 across short, attached and both long spellings, even for empty input; a later zero-width invocation remains valid.
cases.script:
: > empty
for form in split attached long-split long-equals; do
 rc=0
 case $form in
  split) column -c -1 empty || rc=$? ;;
  attached) column -c-1 empty || rc=$? ;;
  long-split) column --output-width -1 empty || rc=$? ;;
  long-equals) column --output-width=-1 empty || rc=$? ;;
 esac
 printf 'negative-status=%s\n' "$rc"
 [[ $rc == 1 ]]
done
printf 'one\n' > data
column -c 0 data
